questions.question: Four identical nodes each advertise 8 whole GPUs. A workload has 36 replicas and each Pod requests one GPU. Ignoring other constraints, how many Pods remain pending?
questions.explanation: The cluster advertises 4 x 8 = 32 integer GPU resources, so 32 Pods can fit and 4 remain pending.

questions.question: Where should a Kubernetes container normally declare an extended GPU resource such as nvidia.com/gpu?
options: In container limits, with an equal request if requests are also specified
Only in nodeSelector
Only in environment variables
As a fractional CPU request
questions.explanation: Kubernetes GPU scheduling treats vendor GPUs as integer extended resources. GPU limits may stand alone because the request defaults to the limit, or matching requests and limits may both be set.

questions.question: What does the device plugin contribute to the scheduling path?
options: It registers the vendor resource, reports healthy devices, and supplies allocation instructions
It trains the model
It chooses Pod priority
It provisions every cluster node
questions.explanation: The kubelet device-plugin framework carries vendor inventory, health, and allocation details without embedding vendor device logic in Kubernetes itself.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes MIG from GPU time slicing?
options: MIG can provide hardware memory and fault isolation; time slicing multiplexes access without those guarantees
Time slicing always reserves equal device memory
MIG is only a scheduler scoring policy
Both modes are fractional CPU requests
questions.explanation: MIG exposes supported hardware partitions with isolation properties. Time slicing advertises shared access replicas and does not isolate device memory or faults between replicas.

questions.question: A Pod requests an available MIG profile but remains Pending. What is the best first diagnostic step?
options: Read scheduler events and inspect the intersection of resources, labels, taints, affinity, and topology constraints
Increase the container image size
Assume the GPU driver is slow
Delete all node labels
questions.explanation: Free aggregate capacity is insufficient if no single node is eligible for the complete Pod contract. Scheduler events expose the failed predicates.

questions.question: Why can a Running time-sliced GPU Pod still have unstable latency?
options: Its advertised token grants shared access, while co-tenants can contend for compute and device memory
Kubernetes converts GPU work to CPU work
The scheduler continuously migrates GPU memory
A Running Pod has no allocated device
questions.explanation: Admission and device assignment do not guarantee a fixed share of compute or memory under time slicing. Operators must measure contention with representative workloads.
